claims.text: The as-cast non-equilibrium alloy contains metastable Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
The initial alloy has a predominantly solid-solution matrix.
The initial alloy has a density below 6 g/cm³.
Controlled high-temperature aging or corrosive exposure transforms metastable Mg-rich intermetallics into more stable phases.
The phase transformation promotes Mg segregation to surfaces and grain boundaries.
Mg segregation fosters formation of a coherent, protective Mg-rich oxide or passivation layer.
The intermetallic transformation changes local chemical potentials and interfacial energy.
Changes in chemical potential and interfacial energy enable a continuous, adherent Mg-rich surface layer to form.
The Mg-rich surface layer shifts the dominant electrochemical and oxidation reactions.
Environmental exposure will increase the stable Mg-rich intermetallic content relative to the as-cast state.
The evolved alloy will develop a coherent, protective oxide layer.
The evolved alloy will have improved high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast alloy.
Improved oxidation resistance will be evidenced by lower weight gain or a more uniform oxide scale.
The evolved alloy will show a measurable corrosion-potential shift and/or a reduced corrosion rate.
The as-cast baseline has a high density of nanoscale Mg-rich intermetallics.
The as-cast baseline lacks the protective oxide scale associated with the proposed transformation.
Substantial differences in initial Mg segregation or metastable-phase distribution may prevent the proposed mechanism.
Excessive environmental severity may disrupt the formation or continuity of the protective layer.
